sections.h2: How does selling a house in West Chicago work?
sections.html:
A West Chicago sale has one local step that most Illinois suburbs lack: the city must approve the structure before a deed can be recorded. You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept an as-is cash purchase, and all three routes run through the same city paperwork. Plan for it early, because the inspection is valid for six months and the city asks for scheduling at least two months before closing.

The city sits on the western edge of DuPage County, about 32 miles from downtown Chicago, with Illinois Route 59 running north and south and Routes 38 and 64 running east and west. Buyers who commute use the Metra station on Main Street or drive to I-88 and I-355. Those access points matter when you describe the house to a buyer, since commute time is usually the first question.

sections.h2: What does the City of West Chicago inspect before a sale?
sections.html:
The Community Development Department inspects the structure for basic maintenance and life safety, and no Deed Certification Number is issued without an approved inspection unless an exemption applies. A visit takes about 30 minutes and happens Monday through Friday between 9 a.m. and 3 p.m. Vacant lots are inspected too.

  • Smoke detectors must be present and working.
  • Ground fault interrupters must be installed where the checklist calls for them.
  • Stair railings must meet the minimum standard.
  • The exterior and yard must meet property maintenance rules, and vacant parcels are checked for tall grass, weeds and garbage.

The fee is a $100.00 base charge plus $0.12 per square foot, using the square footage the township supplies to the city. A vacant parcel adds a flat $20.00. If the house fails, the seller can fix the items and request a re-inspection at no added charge, or sell as-is and leave the repairs to the buyer.

sections.h2: What steps must a West Chicago seller finish before the deed records?
sections.html:
The city lays the steps out in order, and skipping one stalls the recording. The table summarizes them from the city's Property Transactions page.

Seller steps on the City of West Chicago Property Transactions page
OrderStepDetail from the city
1City inspection$100.00 base plus $0.12 per square foot; valid six months
2Final water and sewer readingCall Finance at least 2 working days before closing
3Clear city balancesInspection fees, water bills, parking tickets, ordinance violations, liens, waste services
4Deed Certification NumberForm signed by a seller or agent, presented at 475 Main Street

The number must be attached to the deed when the title is recorded. Payment at City Hall can be made by cash, check, or debit or credit card.

Some transfers are exempt from the inspection fee but still need a certification number. They include new construction, deeds that secure or release a debt, corrective deeds with no added consideration, and a sale where the occupant does not change. A final water reading is still required for those exempt deeds, and the city takes up to five business days to decide an exemption.

sections.h2: What happens if a West Chicago house is sold as-is?
sections.html:
When a seller declines to repair failed items, the buyer signs a Letter of Intent Agreement and posts a $1,600.00 bond with the Community Development Department. The buyer then has 90 days to finish repairs and pass an inspection, and one free 90-day extension is available if requested in person before the deadline. After an approved inspection the city refunds $1,500.00 within two to three weeks, because it keeps a $100.00 administrative fee.

This rule shapes cash offers on rough houses. A buyer who plans renovations can still close, but the bond and the 90-day clock are part of the buyer's cost, so ask any purchaser how they handle the city's requirements before you sign.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about West Chicago homes?
sections.html:
West Chicago has a young, family-heavy housing stock. The Census Bureau counts 7,459 households with 3.35 people each, and 70.9% of homes are owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024. The median owner-occupied home value is $336,800, median gross rent is $1,469, and median household income is $99,927. The July 2025 population estimate is 25,296, down 1.3% from the 2020 base.

  • Median monthly owner costs run $2,428 with a mortgage and $1,035 without one.
  • About 92.2% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is low.
  • Land area is 15.38 square miles, with 1,665.8 people per square mile in 2020.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled when you sell in West Chicago?
sections.html:
West Chicago is in DuPage County, which bills property tax in arrears: the 2025 bills were mailed April 29, 2026, with installments due June 1 and September 1, 2026, and both dates have passed. The county treasurer's page lists the general homestead exemption and the senior exemption at $8,000 each, so check your bill for both. If a mortgage servicer pays your tax, a yellow box on the bill says so and you should not pay twice.

At closing the title company prorates the tax between seller and buyer, and Illinois adds a state transfer tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value stated in the declaration, under 35 ILCS 200/31-10. Ask the DuPage County recorder what the county adds. Illinois also requires a seller of one to four units to deliver a completed disclosure report before the contract is signed, under 765 ILCS 77/20.

sections.h2: What should a landlord know before selling a West Chicago rental?
sections.html: West Chicago requires a Rental Property License for residential landlords and annual rental inspections against the International Property Maintenance Code. If you own a rental you are selling, confirm that your license and inspection record are current, because open city items surface at the same Community Development counter that handles the sale inspection. Tenants stay in place through a sale unless the lease says otherwise, so ask the Community Development Department how a change of occupant affects your exemption options.

sections.h2: What is West Chicago like for sellers and buyers?
sections.html:
The place began as a railroad junction. The Galena and Chicago Union reached the site in 1849 and the Aurora Branch crossed it in 1850, which made it the first railroad junction west of Chicago. It was platted as Junction in 1855, incorporated as the Village of Turner in 1873 and renamed West Chicago in 1896. The 2020 census counted 25,614 residents.

Local employers include Jel Sert and Ball Horticultural Company, and the city lists West Chicago Elementary School District 33 and Community High School District 94 among its larger employers. DuPage Airport sits inside the city limits, and the West Chicago Prairie Forest Preserve and the Illinois Prairie Path give buyers trail access. The park district manages more than 390 acres across 13 sites, led by 125-acre Reed-Keppler Park.

faqs.q: Do I need a city inspection to sell my house in West Chicago?
faqs.a: Yes, unless the transfer is exempt. The city will not issue a Deed Certification Number without an approved inspection, and the inspection costs $100.00 plus $0.12 per square foot. It stays valid for six months, so schedule it about two months before closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Chicago house that fails the inspection?
faqs.a: Yes. You can repair the items and get a free re-inspection, or sell as-is. With an as-is sale the buyer posts a $1,600.00 bond and has 90 days to finish repairs and pass.

faqs.q: Who schedules the final water reading in West Chicago?
faqs.a: The seller does. Contact the city's Finance Department at least 2 working days before closing, pay the unbilled water and sewer use, and clear any other city balances before the certification number is issued.

faqs.q: Does West Chicago charge a local transfer tax?
faqs.a: The Property Transactions page describes inspection fees and a Deed Certification Number but no local transfer tax rate. The state tax is 50 cents per $500 of value, and the DuPage County recorder can tell you what the county adds.

faqs.q: When are DuPage County property tax bills due?
faqs.a: Illinois bills a year behind, and the 2025 bills carried installment dates of June 1 and September 1, 2026. Both have passed. Your closing statement splits the unpaid portion between seller and buyer.
